sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Commands and dependencies
sections.what: Declares the package name, the commands for generating types, collecting artefacts, building, running, rendering text and testing, and the libraries the viewer needs.
sections.why: The description says the viewer only reads artefacts. The commands make sure those artefacts are current before the build runs.
sections.watch_out: The build and test steps collect whatever artefacts are on disk, so results depend on what the last replay wrote.

summary: Lists the viewer's name, its libraries, and the commands that generate types, collect results, build, run and test it.
purpose: Defines the commands developers and CI run, in order, to produce the viewer and check it.
why: The description says the viewer has no backend, no network access and no model calls. The scripts chain generation and collection before building, so the build uses fresh inputs.
how: 1. The dev and build commands run type generation and artefact collection first, through their pre-steps. 2. The build runs a type check and then a bundle. 3. The test command collects artefacts and then runs vitest. 4. The libraries are React and its DOM library, plus TypeScript, Vite, the test runner and a schema-to-types tool.
inputs: Packages from the npm registry, the scripts under scripts/, and the JSON schema in packages/schema.
outputs: Commands for generating types, checking types, collecting artefacts, building, running a dev server, rendering text, and testing.
risks: The pre-steps regenerate types and collect artefacts, so a failure there stops the build. Version ranges use caret syntax, so a fresh install can pull newer minor versions. The lock file is not in the packet.
debug: If a script fails, run its step alone to find which part broke. For type errors, run the type check command. For missing data, run the collect command. A mismatch between generated types and the schema shows up in the type check.
